recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is. Future Contract changes should be handled against the current Contract.term/offer/securityLabel model, or through any separately applied Contract removal/refactoring decision, rather than by backporting the obsolete 2017 spreadsheet paths.
issue_request: FHIR-12860 was a Published/Persuasive Financial Management change request for the Contract resource, raised and applied for DSTU2. It asked for new Contract derivation and decision fields, securityLabels similar to ConsentDirective, and making topic a structure after Financial Management teleconference approval on February 19, 2017.
initial_application: Historical source commits 054d53ac1c, 43e53248d6, and c6671a62a7 were tagged with the pre-migration #12860 tracker number. They updated the old Contract spreadsheet source and related terminology inputs for Contract structure, content derivative, decision, and term securityLabel support.
additional_context: Contract is active in source/fhir.ini. Later published same-family work, especially FHIR-13403 and the already-published FHIR-12893 audit on the combined branch, explains why the original obsolete decisionType/header paths are no longer the current source shape. Current Contract source carries the applied concepts at Contract.contentDerivative, Contract.topic[x]/Contract.term.topic[x], Contract.term.securityLabel and securityLabelNumber links, and Contract.term.offer.decision/decisionMode.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active Contract source already preserves the semantic requirements from FHIR-12860 after later Contract refactoring, and reintroducing old root/header element names would duplicate or contradict the current model.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Contract decision-type issue already has a no-change audit on the combined branch and confirms the decision concept now lives at Contract.term.offer.decision.
Published/Persuasive Ricardian Contract refactor already has a fixed commit on the combined branch and explains the later Contract term/offer structure used by current source.
Later Contract removal work exists on a separate branch, but it is not in the current combined branch and does not alter this current-source audit.
